source: Original (no calculator). Express expressions in form ln k, k in Z+.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Express ln 8 + ln 9 in the form ln k.
parts.notes: A1 for ln 72 (single application of the product rule ln a + ln b = ln(ab)).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Express 2 ln 6 - ln 4 in the form ln k.
parts.tolerance: Accept ln 9. Intermediate ln 36 - ln 4 or ln(36/4) acceptable.
parts.notes: A1 for 2 ln 6 = ln 36 (power rule). A1 for ln(36/4) = ln 9 (quotient rule).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Express ln 48 - 2 ln 2 - ln 3 in the form ln k.
parts.tolerance: Accept ln 4. Any valid order of product/quotient/power-rule applications is acceptable.
parts.notes: A1 for combining 2 ln 2 = ln 4 (or equivalent intermediate such as ln(2 ln 2 + ln 3) = ln 12). A1 for the final answer ln 4.

source: Original (no calculator). Solve exponential and logarithmic equations.

parts.label: a
parts.notes: M1 for rewriting 27 = 3^3 and equating exponents (2x = 3). A1 for x = 3/2.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept x = 5 only. The candidate must reject x = -5 (outside x > 3) either implicitly or explicitly.
parts.notes: M1 for combining logs as log_2[(x+3)(x-3)] = 4 (product rule). A1 for exponentiating and simplifying to x^2 - 9 = 16 (or x^2 = 25). A1 for x = 5 (with x = -5 rejected by the domain constraint x > 3).

source: Original. Asymptote, x-intercept, and inverse of g(x) = 2 + log_3(x - 1).

parts.label: a
parts.description: State the equation of the vertical asymptote of g(x) = 2 + log_3(x - 1).
parts.tolerance: Accept x = 1 only. Do not accept '1' alone (the answer is the equation of a line, not a value).
parts.notes: A1 for x = 1 (argument of the log = 0).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the x-intercept of g(x) = 2 + log_3(x - 1).
parts.tolerance: Accept x = 10/9, x ≈ 1.11 (3 s.f.), or the ordered pair (10/9, 0).
parts.notes: M1 for setting g(x) = 0 and isolating log_3(x - 1) = -2. A1 for x = 10/9 (or equivalent).

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 1 + 3^(x - 2), 1 + 3^x/9, or any algebraically equivalent form.
parts.notes: M1 for interchanging x and y and writing x = 2 + log_3(y - 1) (or equivalent setup). A1 for exponentiating to y - 1 = 3^(x - 2). A1 for the final inverse g^{-1}(x) = 1 + 3^(x - 2).

source: Original. Continuous exponential growth A(t) = 8 e^(kt), A(4) = 32.

parts.label: a
parts.tolerance: Show that (answer given). Accept any equivalent intermediate, e.g. k = (ln 4)/4 = (2 ln 2)/4.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting A(4) = 32 and isolating e^(4k) = 4. A1 for taking ln to get 4k = ln 4 = 2 ln 2. AG label on the simplification to (1/2) ln 2 (no separate mark).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find A(11), correct to the nearest integer.
parts.tolerance: Accept 362 only for the nearest integer. The exact form 256√2 is acceptable as the M1 step.
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t = 11 to obtain A(11) = 8 e^(11k) = 8 · 2^(11/2) = 256√2 (or evaluating numerically). A1 for 362 kg.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the time at which the mass first reaches 1000 kg, correct to 2 d.p.
parts.tolerance: Accept 13.93. The exact form t = 6 log_2(5) or t = (2 ln 125)/(ln 2) is acceptable as the M1 step. A direct GDC solve of 8 e^(kt) = 1000 also acceptable.
parts.notes: M1 for setting 8 e^(kt) = 1000 and arriving at t = ln(125)/k (or equivalent). A1 for 13.93.

source: Original. Compound interest, nominal annual 4.8% compounded monthly, P = $5000.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down a formula for V(t).
parts.tolerance: Accept either the un-simplified (1 + 0.048/12) form or the simplified (1.004) form. Exponent must be 12t, not t.
parts.notes: A1 for any correct compound-interest formula with monthly compounding: V(t) = 5000(1 + 0.048/12)^(12t) or V(t) = 5000(1.004)^(12t).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find V(6), correct to the nearest cent.
parts.tolerance: Accept $6664.95 or $6664.96 (full-precision GDC evaluation rounds to either depending on intermediate precision).
parts.notes: M1 for substituting t = 6 to get V(6) = 5000(1.004)^72. A1 for $6664.95 (or $6664.96).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the smallest number of full years for V(t) to first exceed $8000.
parts.tolerance: Accept n = 10. Do not accept 9.81 years as the final answer because full years are required. Alternative method (table search) acceptable: full marks if both adjacent rows are shown (V(9) = $7695.03 and V(10) = $8072.62); award full marks for a single-row table too, but attach a feedback note recommending the adjacent row.
parts.notes: M1 for setting 5000(1.004)^(12n) > 8000 (or 1.004^(12n) > 1.6) or an equivalent logarithmic/evaluation method. A1 for the boundary value n > 9.81... (or, for the table method, for both adjacent rows). A1 for the smallest full-year value n = 10. If the student uses a single-row table, attach feedback: 'Show both adjacent rows (n=9 and n=10) to justify the crossover.' See markscheme-spec.md §18.

source: Original. Decibel scale L = 10 log_10(I/I_0), I_0 = 10^-12 W/m^2.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find L for a vacuum cleaner of intensity I = 3.2 × 10^-5 W/m^2, correct to 1 d.p.
parts.tolerance: Accept 75.1 only for 1 d.p. The full-precision value 75.0515... is acceptable as the M1 step.
parts.notes: M1 for computing I/I_0 = 3.2 × 10^7 (or equivalent setup). A1 for 75.1 dB.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find I when L = 130 dB. Express in the form a × 10^k with 1 ≤ a < 10, k in Z.
parts.tolerance: Accept I = 1 × 10^1 or I = 10 W/m^2. The form a × 10^k is satisfied by a = 1, k = 1; no separate 'a = 1, k = 1' line is required.
parts.notes: M1 for inverting the formula to log_10(I/10^-12) = 13. A1 for I = 10 W/m^2 (i.e. 1 × 10^1).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Show that doubling the intensity increases L by approximately 3.01 dB.
parts.tolerance: Show that (answer given). Accept any valid derivation that produces 10 log_10(2) as the L-difference.
parts.notes: M1 for setting up L_{2I} - L_I = 10 log_10(2I/I_0) - 10 log_10(I/I_0) and simplifying to 10 log_10(2). A1 for evaluating 10 log_10(2) = 3.0103... AG label on ≈ 3.01 dB (no separate mark).
